chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halby, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man who led a group in the Asr prayer, and he remembered while he was praying that he had not prayed the first [prayer]. He (peace be upon him) said: 'So let him consider the missed one as the first, and let him resume after it the Asr prayer, and the people have already completed their prayer.'
ai.seo_question: What should an Imam do if he realizes he missed a prayer while leading the congregation?
ai.summary: This ruling from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes the principle of *Tartib* (sequential order) in making up missed prayers, even when the missed prayer is discovered during the current one. It highlights the Imam's unique responsibility to maintain the structural integrity of the prayer sequence for himself, while the congregation's status is determined by their adherence to his lead, reflecting the Shia emphasis on the validity of individual *Qada* prayers performed in their proper chronological order.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al Halby who said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullahasws about a man leading a group in Al-Asr Salāt, so he remembers while he is praying that he had not prayed the former Salāt. Heasws said: ‘So let him make it to be the former which had been missed out, and let him resume after Al-Asr Salāt, and the people proceeded with their Salāts’.
en.sarwar: 7. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘ Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabiy who has said the following: “

I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a man who leads people for al-‘Asr, then he remembers during Salah (prayer) that he has not performed the one before. He (the Imam) said, ‘He considers it (Salah (prayer) he is performing) as the one before which is missed and thereafter perform al-‘Asr again and the people proceed with their Salah (prayer).”’
